distinguishing_features: Embeds a concentric, radially graded dielectric layer (permittivity varying from inner to outer sleeve) inside the oil-filled bushing interior to flatten the internal DC field
Uses multi-material co-molded silicone-epoxy/epoxy construction rather than monitoring or predictive inference
Targets internal conductor/insulation interface field peaks and space-charge-driven partial discharge as the degradation driver, independent of external creepage
Passive material/architecture design change requiring no sensors, telemetry, or computation
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce internal electric-field peaks and space-charge accumulation at the conductor/insulation interface of an oil-filled HVDC bushing so as to suppress ionization and partial discharge that precede insulation breakdown, without enlarging the external creepage path.
parsed.viable_reason: As written the physics is broken: permittivity units are given as F/m (k=5.0 is dimensionless), the stated graded-field reduction formula is not a valid Laplace field solution, and the claimed >50% E_max reduction ignores that the DC resistive field distribution is governed by conductivity, not permittivity.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Transferring concentric radial field-grading from stator end-winding stress-grading to an HVDC bushing's internal field homogenization is not a routine parameter tweak of any cited monitoring/predictive prior art.
